section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1993
title: ACCIDENTAL DEATHS & SUICIDES IN INDIA - 1993 N.C.R.B.- 55 2.5.4 The Frequency distribution of suicides in States/UTs/Cities by various ‘Means’ is given in APPENDIX-V. However, the details of percentage distribution of the same are given in APPENDIX-VII. On careful examination, it is observed that ‘Poison’ was the most prominent (having highest percentage share) means in as many as 14 states and 1 UT while ‘Hanging’ (next common means of suicide) was prominent in other 9 states & 3 UTs. In addition, ‘Hanging’ was the only means of suicide in Mizoram. In the UT of Daman & Diu, suicides due to both these means were equally distributed. However, in Delhi UT, ‘Fire’ was the most frequent means of suicide. The tabular and the graphical representation of deaths due to ‘Poisoning’ and ‘Hanging’ are presented below.
